The cloak is made of several homogeneous and anisotropic segments, with no extreme values of material parameters involved.
A linear homogeneous transformation method is applied in each segment to transform a large hidden region into a much smaller one.
The simplified hexagonal cloak is fabricated using six calcite trapezoids glued together, with the optic axis in each trapezoid parallel to its sides.
The inner radius of the simplified cloak is 1.5 mm, the outer radius is 13 cm, and the height is 13 mm.
The inner surfaces of the cloak are coated with silver.
The cloak is immersed in a transparent, light yellow liquid with a refractive index of 1.72 at 589.3 nm.
In the experimental demonstration, a 1.3 mm yellow column is used as the hidden object inside the cloak.
The cloak is able to guide light around the hidden object, making it invisible to an observer.
The cloak can manipulate laser beams incident from different angles, guiding them around the hidden object without any deviation.
The theoretical analysis shows that the proposed polygonal cloak can be rendered invisible to rays incident from all directions.
The simplified hexagonal cloak works for six incident directions, while the theoretically proposed polygonal cloak can work for rays incident from all directions.
The lost performance in the simplified cloak is due to the removal of the highly anisotropic Segment I materials.
The linear homogeneous transformation method used in the cloak design can be useful for future cloak designs with different shapes and applications.
The experimental demonstration is a new step towards feasible human cloaking devices.
The cloak is able to conceal the hidden object in the whole visible spectrum.
